reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega and E be measurable spaces, mu a probability measure on Omega, X:R x Omega -> E with every slice X(t,.) measurable, g:E->R measurable, and A:R x E->R with every state slice A(v,.) measurable. Fix arbitrary real a,b. Assume g(X(a,.)) and g(X(b,.)) are mu-integrable and (v,omega) -> A(v,X(v,omega)) is integrable for (Lebesgue restricted to (min(a,b),max(a,b)]) product mu. Suppose Z:Omega->R is integrable with integral zero and, for mu-almost every omega, g(X(b,omega))-g(X(a,omega)) = Integral_a^b A(v,X(v,omega)) dv + Z(omega), using oriented interval integrals. Define rho(t)=(X(t,.))_*mu. Then Integral_E g d rho(b) - Integral_E g d rho(a) = Integral_a^b [Integral_E A(v,x) d rho(v)(x)] dv. No ordering of a and b is required.
objects: Measurable spaces Omega and E, probability mu, slice-measurable process X, measurable g, and state-slice-measurable drift A.
Fixed real endpoints a,b; integrable centered random variable Z.
Marginals rho(t)=mu.map(X(t,.)); endpoint g-expectations and time-dependent A-expectations.
domains: All times are real, without nonnegativity constraints.
Product integrability uses the time-first domain R x Omega.
Set.uIoc a b is (min(a,b),max(a,b)], whereas Integral_a^b is oriented.
quantifiers: For every real t, X(t,.) is measurable; for every real v, A(v,.) is measurable.
The endpoint identity holds for mu-almost every omega for the given a,b and Z.
All data satisfying these assumptions yield the displayed identity; no single Z for all endpoint pairs is asserted.
assumptions: g is measurable; its compositions at a and b are integrable.
The composition A(v,X(v,omega)) is integrable on the specified product measure, including AE strong measurability.
Z is integrable and has exactly zero mean.
The sample increment identity holds AE in omega.
No separate joint-measurability assumption for X or A, continuity, compactness, filtration or martingale property is present.
conclusion: Difference of g-integrals against true marginal laws at b and a equals the oriented time integral of A(v,.) against the true law at v.
The three hidden maps in order are X b, X a and X v, as supplied in the approved context.
scopes: The product-integrability hypothesis is restricted to the unordered half-open interval; no global-in-time drift integrability is asserted.
Fubini yields section integrability for almost every time, not necessarily every time.
The variable v inside the outer integral also determines the marginal rho(v); it is not a fixed endpoint law.
constant_dependencies: No numerical constants or norm estimates appear.
Z is part of the data for the fixed endpoints and may depend on those endpoints; no joint selection is specified.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: Endpoint law integrals are genuinely integrable by the endpoint hypotheses and measurable pushforward formula. Drift sections are integrable for AE time in uIoc by product integrability; at exceptional times the inner real integral retains Lean's totalized value (zero if nonintegrable). The oriented outer integral has genuine integrability. Path drift is integrable for AE omega.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: The increment identity is AE omega for the fixed pair a,b. Section integrability in v or omega obtained from Fubini is AE, not pointwise.
semantic_checks.pushforwards: Approved context explicitly identifies the three marginal maps by X b, X a, X v. Omitted trailing arguments are proofs of measurability, not unidentified random variables.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: If a<=b, Integral_a^b is the usual integral over (a,b]; if b<a, it is minus the integral over (b,a]. Product integrability always uses uIoc, independent of orientation.
semantic_checks.exponents: No powers, p-moments, or squared increments.
semantic_checks.compactness: Neither sample nor state space is assumed topological or compact.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: a=b is allowed: both endpoint difference and oriented integral are zero. No time is required to be positive.
semantic_checks.absolute_continuity: This single increment identity does not itself assert any absolute-continuity property of a time curve.
